MANILA, Philippines — The local government of Tarlac City has suspended classes and school-based work for Tuesday, Oct. 6, from kindergarten to high school to commemorate Teachers’ Day.

Mayor Susan Yap issued Executive Order No. 50 to provide teachers and students enough time and opportunity to participate in the National Teachers’ Day and World Teachers’ Day celebrations of the Tarlac City Schools Division (TCSD).

READ: Palace: No nationwide class suspension for Teachers’ Day on Oct. 5

Ma. Irelyn Tamayo, TCSD’s superintendent, has sent a letter to Yap on Sunday, Oct. 4, informing her of the activities that the schools division office has slated to commemorate this year’s Teachers’ Day. /cb

BAYAMBANG, Pangasinan – Onsite classes in this central Pangasinan town are suspended on Friday, Oct. 9, to allow teachers to attend a municipal-wide celebration of World Teachers’ Day.

Schools will shift to asynchronous learning and modular distance learning to ensure that students continue their studies during the suspension.

Bayambang Mayor Mary Clare Phyllis Judith Jose Quaimbao signed Executive Order No. 164-2026 on Thursday, Oct. 8, citing the need to recognize teachers’ dedication, sacrifices and service to learners.

School heads, teachers and education authorities were directed to ensure learning continuity through appropriate activities, instructional materials, modules, assignments and other tasks that students can complete through asynchronous or modular arrangements. /dp
